conbody.p: The critical path is the chain of tasks that decides when the plan ends: each has no room to slip, so a day lost on any of them is a day lost at the end. OpenV works out, for every task with dates, its float: how many days it could slip before the plan's last task would end later. A task can slip until the plan's last day, or until it would push a task it drives:

ul.li: a finish to start relationship lets it slip until the day before the other task starts;
a start to start relationship lets its start slip until the other task's start;
a finish to finish relationship lets its end slip until the other task's end.

conbody.p: A task with no float, and not yet done, is critical. With Critical path on, which it is when the page opens, critical tasks have an amber outline and an amber dot in the outline, and the arrows between them are amber and heavier. A task's panel says Critical, or how many days of float it has. The float is worked out from the dates as they stand: OpenV does not move tasks for you. A task with no relationships has float up to the plan's last day, so only relationships make a path longer than one task.
